response.sql: WITH b AS (SELECT o.timespan AS ts, COUNT(*) AS c FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), s AS (SELECT ts, c, c * 1.0 / SUM(c) OVER () AS share FROM b), a AS (SELECT ts, c, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(c) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share_of_kept, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_avg_share FROM a WHERE share > avg_share

assumptions.assumption: A bucket's count is the number of matched riskandmargin rows (inner join to orders) with that timespan value; NULL timespan forms its own bucket via GROUP BY.
The 'average share' used as the threshold is the mean share across all buckets (equal to 1/number of buckets), not just the kept ones.
'How far above the average share they are on average' is the mean of (bucket share minus the all-bucket average share) over the kept buckets.
